thread:
Nina (marketing): Heads-up: ops just flagged a potential regional degradation in ap-south. We should agree on statuspage copy, email cadence, and whether we pull in legal for wording. Goal: clear, concise, consistent across channels. Thoughts?
Carlos (ops): Short answer: yes. For suspected degradations we'll post an initial 'investigating' status within 10 minutes. If impact persists beyond 45 minutes, ops will call for an email. We'll include an ETA only if we have one.
Priya (support): Support wants a one-line subject and a 2-sentence body for the email so account teams can forward quickly. Also need canned Slack replies and a short FAQ for CS reps (retry guidance, mitigation steps).
Ravi (legal): Quick note: avoid absolute promises (e.g., "service fully restored by X"). Use conditional language and include data-handling reassurance if customers ask about logs. I'll review any customer-facing templates.
Maya (product): For customers using private deployments, include a line clarifying this is a hosted-region issue and private/on-prem customers aren't affected unless we explicitly say otherwise. Also tag pinned-model customers for targeted CS outreach.
Owen (growth): Social playbook: only post a short status-signal once we have the statuspage live. No speculation on X/Twitter. If incident goes >3h we mobilize a short post-mortem thread and an email offering a sync with affected customers.
Nina (marketing): Proposed statuspage structure (short bullets): 1) What we're seeing, 2) Who's affected (regions & features), 3) What we're doing, 4) Suggested action for customers, 5) Next update ETA. Example headline: "Investigating degraded inference in ap-south". Keep it simple.
Carlos (ops): I'll draft a baseline 'investigating' message. Can we agree on tone? My vote: straightforward + empathetic, no blame, call out workarounds if available.
Priya (support): Tone: "We're investigating an issue affecting inference requests in ap-south. You may see increased latency or errors. Our team is working to restore normal service. Please retry and contact support if you see persistent failures." Keep versions: micro (one-liner), email (short paragraph), FAQ (3 Qs).
Nina (marketing): Micro status for status page: "Investigating degraded inference in ap-south. Some requests may fail or be slower. We're investigating and will update shortly." Email subject options: "Redwood: Investigating inference disruptions in ap-south" or shorter "Redwood: ap-south service notice". Pick one.
Ravi (legal): Both look fine. Prefer the shorter subject for high-volume emails. Add privacy line in footer: "No customer data exposure is suspected at this time." (we can remove if investigation shows otherwise).
Maya (product): Add a short ticket template for account teams to report severe customer impact: includes customer org, model pinned? yes/no, request IDs if available, and top-line impact. We'll push these to CS triage.
Owen (growth): For social, suggested copy once status page is live: "We're investigating an issue affecting inference in ap-south — details: <statuspage link>. We'll post updates there." Keep it as a pointer.
Carlos (ops): Decision on thresholds: status page <=10m, email at 45m, account exec outreach at 2h for top 25 customers. Ops will ping #marketing with the signal "ops:send-email" and include the incident summary.
Priya (support): I'll prepare canned replies now and upload to the CS playbook. Will include both short and expanded variants and a plain-text email body.
Nina (marketing): I'll draft the email and the statuspage versions, post them in this thread. Please review quickly. Also I'll prepare a pre-approved set of subject lines and preheaders to speed send.
watchdog-bot: incident_watch -> alert created for region ap-south at 2026-05-02T09:45:00Z
Carlos (ops): Thanks. I'll post the ops draft in ~20m. If we go to email, please do not send any marketing promotional content — keep it incident-only.
Nina (marketing): Agreed — incident-only. Also let's confirm whether we should include estimated impact metrics (e.g., % of requests failing). My preference: only include metrics if they're reliable.
Ravi (legal): Agreed with conservative metrics policy. Avoid giving precise percentages unless monitoring is validated. We can say "a subset of customers" or "significant increase in errors".
Maya (product): Putting together the pinned-model list now and will DM Priya with the first pass.
Owen (growth): I'll draft social templates and a short note for account teams to use on their outreach.
Priya (support): Uploaded CS canned replies to the playbook and linked them here: https://playbook.example/incident-cs.
Nina (marketing): Thank you. Once Carlos posts the ops text I'll edit for clarity and then stand by for the ops signal to send email. Action owners: ops -> ops draft + signal (Carlos), marketing -> email + status edits (Nina), support -> canned replies + CS FAQ (Priya), legal -> wording review (Ravi), product -> pinned-customer list (Maya), growth -> social/account templates (Owen).
Carlos (ops): Draft posted in #ops in 10m. We'll rehearse this flow in tomorrow's incident tabletop at 11:00. Invite sent.
Nina (marketing): Great, talk after the draft. Thanks everyone.
